general_tips: Download from the game's official mod site or a well-known site below, or from the author's own page.
Avoid 'mirror' sites that re-upload other people's mods. They're often full of ads and fake download buttons, and sometimes malware.
A real mod is almost never an .exe file. If a download is a program you have to run, be very careful.
Check that the mod is made for your game version, and read its requirements: many mods need another mod installed first.
After adding mods, press Scan in ModTender to catch duplicates, broken downloads and missing requirements.

sources.name: ModHub
sources.note: GIANTS' own mod site, also built into the game. Every mod is tested by GIANTS before release.

sources.name: Creators' own pages
sources.note: Many modders also publish on their own website, itch.io, Patreon or GitHub. These aren't tested by GIANTS, but they come straight from the author.

tips: Leave mods zipped: Farming Simulator reads the .zip directly.
File names must only use letters, numbers and underscores. ModTender fixes this for you.
Lots of 'FS25 mods' websites copy ModHub mods and wrap them in ads. If a mod is on ModHub, download it there.

sources.name: ModHub
sources.note: GIANTS' own mod site, also built into the game. Every mod is tested by GIANTS before release.

tips: Make sure a mod says FS22: FS25 mods don't work in FS22 and the other way around.
Leave mods zipped: Farming Simulator reads the .zip directly.

sources.name: Modrinth
sources.note: Open-source mod site with a clean, fast launcher-friendly catalogue. Some popular mods (like Sodium) are mainly published here.

sources.name: CurseForge
sources.note: The biggest Minecraft mod and modpack site, with its own app for installing modpacks.

sources.name: Fabric
sources.note: Mod loader for Fabric mods. Most Fabric mods also need Fabric API.

sources.name: NeoForge
sources.note: Mod loader for NeoForge mods (most big modpacks on 1.21 use it).

sources.name: Forge
sources.note: The original mod loader, used by older versions and many classic modpacks.

sources.name: StopModReposts
sources.note: Explains which sites copy mods without permission, and offers a browser extension that warns you.

tips: Every mod must match your Minecraft version AND your loader (Fabric, Forge or NeoForge).
In a modpack, let the pack's app (CurseForge or Modrinth) manage updates. Adding or removing mods by hand can break the pack.

sources.name: SMAPI
sources.note: The mod loader almost every Stardew mod needs. Install it first.

sources.name: Nexus Mods
sources.note: Where most Stardew Valley mods are published.

sources.name: ModDrop
sources.note: Smaller site where some Stardew authors publish too.

sources.name: CurseForge
sources.note: Some Stardew mods are published here as well.

tips: Content packs (folders whose name starts with [CP], [JA] and so on) need their framework mod, like Content Patcher. ModTender flags it if one is missing.
SMAPI's log (smapi.io/log) is the quickest way to see why a mod isn't loading.

sources.name: Nexus Mods
sources.note: The main home of Skyrim SE / Anniversary Edition mods.

sources.name: Creations
sources.note: Bethesda's official mod and Creation Club store, also in the game's menu.

sources.name: SKSE
sources.note: Script extender many big mods need. Must match your exact game version.

sources.name: Mod Organizer 2
sources.note: Load-order manager that keeps your game folder clean. Recommended for large mod lists.

tips: Game updates often break SKSE plugins. If mods stop working after an update, wait for them to update too.
Load order matters: mods lower in the list win when two change the same thing.

sources.name: Nexus Mods
sources.note: The main home of Fallout 4 mods.

sources.name: Creations
sources.note: Bethesda's official mod and Creation Club store, also in the game's menu.

sources.name: F4SE
sources.note: Script extender many big mods need. Must match your exact game version.

tips: Fallout 4's Next-Gen update split mods into old-gen and next-gen versions. Pick the one that matches your game.

sources.name: Nexus Mods
sources.note: Where most Witcher 3 mods are published, including the big overhauls and the tools below.

sources.name: Steam Workshop
sources.note: Official Workshop for mods made with REDkit. Subscribing installs them for you (Steam version only).

sources.name: Community Patch - Shared Imports
sources.note: Required by many script mods. Install it whenever a mod lists it as a requirement.

sources.name: Script Merger
sources.note: Merges script mods that change the same game files, so they don't cancel each other out.

sources.name: REDkit
sources.note: CD PROJEKT RED's free official mod editor, for making your own mods. You don't need it just to play mods.

tips: Mods go in the game's 'mods' folder, and each mod folder's name must start with 'mod'. Folders whose names start with 'dlc' go in the game's 'dlc' folder instead.
Make sure a mod supports your version: Next-Gen (4.x) and the old 1.32 version need different mods.
Some mods also include a 'bin' folder with settings files: copy it into the game folder as the instructions say.
Keep Steam Workshop subscriptions and hand-installed mods separate, and run Script Merger after adding script mods.
The Witcher 4 isn't out yet. Mods made for The Witcher 3 won't work with it.

sources.name: Nexus Mods
sources.note: Where nearly all Cyberpunk 2077 mods are published.

sources.name: Cyber Engine Tweaks
sources.note: Framework many script mods need. Others need RED4ext, ArchiveXL or TweakXL: check each mod's requirements.

tips: After a game patch, framework mods usually need an update first. Update those before anything else.

sources.name: In-game Mod Manager (mod.io)
sources.note: Larian's official mod browser, on the game's main menu. Works on PC, Mac and consoles.

sources.name: Nexus Mods
sources.note: Bigger selection, including mods that can't be on the official browser.

sources.name: BG3 Mod Manager
sources.note: Community load-order tool for Nexus mods. Its GitHub page is the only official download.

tips: Turning on mods disables achievements in Baldur's Gate 3.
Mods from the official browser are managed by the game. Don't move them around by hand.

sources.name: Thunderstore
sources.note: Where most Valheim mods live. Its r2modman app installs them for you.

sources.name: BepInExPack for Valheim
sources.note: The mod loader every Valheim mod needs. Take this exact package.

sources.name: Nexus Mods
sources.note: Some Valheim mods are published here too.

tips: Valheim 1.0 (September 2026) broke many older mods. Check a mod was updated after that before installing it.
In multiplayer, client-and-server mods must be installed by every player and on the server.

sources.name: Steam Workshop
sources.note: Where nearly all RimWorld mods are published. Subscribing installs and updates them.

sources.name: RimSort
sources.note: Free mod-order manager that sorts mods and warns about problems.

tips: Many mods need Harmony and must load near the top of the list.
Check each mod supports your RimWorld version (1.5, 1.6…).

sources.name: Steam Workshop
sources.note: The easiest place to get Euro Truck Simulator 2 mods: subscribe and they install themselves.

sources.name: SCS Software forum
sources.note: Official forum where many map and truck mods are announced and supported.

tips: Map mods often need to be in a specific order in the in-game Mod Manager. Follow the author's instructions.

sources.name: Steam Workshop
sources.note: The easiest place to get American Truck Simulator mods: subscribe and they install themselves.

sources.name: SCS Software forum
sources.note: Official forum where many map and truck mods are announced and supported.

tips: Map mods often need to be in a specific order in the in-game Mod Manager. Follow the author's instructions.

sources.name: CurseForge
sources.note: Large Sims 4 mod and custom content site with its own app for installing and updating.

sources.name: Mod The Sims
sources.note: One of the oldest Sims mod communities, with moderated uploads.

tips: Turn on 'Enable Custom Content and Mods' and 'Script Mods Allowed' in the game's Options → Other.
Script mods (.ts4script) only load from the Mods folder or one folder below it. .package files can go up to 5 folders deep.
After every game patch, script mods often break. Check each mod's page for an update before playing.

sources.name: Paradox Mods
sources.note: The only official mod platform for Cities: Skylines II. Also built into the game's main menu.

tips: Cities: Skylines II doesn't use the Steam Workshop, and mods for the first game don't work in it.

sources.name: mod.io
sources.note: SnowRunner's official mod platform. Subscribe on the site or in the game's mod browser.

tips: You need a mod.io account linked in the game's Mods menu before subscribed mods download.

eldenring.name: Elden Ring

sources.name: Nexus Mods
sources.note: Where most Elden Ring mods are published.

sources.name: Mod Engine 2
sources.note: Loads mods without changing the game's own files. Many mods need it.

tips: Never play online with mods: Easy Anti-Cheat can ban your account. Play mods offline, or with Seamless Co-op's separate setup.
Keep a backup of your save before trying overhaul mods.

terraria.name: Terraria

sources.name: tModLoader
sources.note: Free on Steam and needed for almost all Terraria mods. It has its own in-game mod browser.

sources.name: Steam Workshop (tModLoader)
sources.note: Where tModLoader mods are published. Subscribing installs them.

tips: tModLoader keeps separate characters and worlds, so your vanilla saves aren't touched.

lethalcompany.name: Lethal Company

sources.name: Thunderstore
sources.note: Where nearly all Lethal Company mods live. Use r2modman or the Thunderstore app to install them.

tips: Everyone in a lobby usually needs the same mods. Share a mod-manager profile code with friends.
Game updates often break mods. Wait for the mods to update before you update the game.

satisfactory.name: Satisfactory

sources.name: Satisfactory Mod Repository (ficsit.app)
sources.note: The community's official mod site, with Satisfactory Mod Manager for installing.

tips: Use Satisfactory Mod Manager (linked from ficsit.app) instead of copying files by hand: it handles dependencies.

sources.name: Nexus Mods
sources.note: The biggest general mod site, covering thousands of games.

sources.name: mod.io
sources.note: Official mod platform for many games, often built into the game.

sources.name: Thunderstore
sources.note: Popular for Unity games such as Lethal Company, R.E.P.O. and Risk of Rain 2.

sources.name: Steam Workshop
sources.note: If your game supports it, subscribing installs and updates mods automatically.

tips: Search for '<game name> official mods' first: many games have their own mod site.

sources.name: Steam Workshop
sources.note: Where nearly all Arma 3 mods live. Subscribe, then tick them in the Arma 3 Launcher.

sources.name: CBA_A3
sources.note: Community Base Addons: the library most Arma 3 mods need. Load it first.

sources.name: Arma 3 Launcher presets
sources.note: Groups share their mods as a Launcher preset (.html). Open it with Match mods in ModTender to see what you're missing.

tips: When you join a modded server, load exactly its mod list. Use the server's preset, not your own selection.
If a server checks signatures, every mod needs a .bikey key. ModTender warns about mods without one.

sources.name: Arma Reforger Workshop (in game)
sources.note: Reforger mods come from Bohemia's own workshop, not Steam. Download them from the Workshop menu in the game.

sources.name: Workshop website
sources.note: Browse mods, read changelogs and find a mod's ID for a server's config.json.

tips: Joining a modded server downloads its mods automatically. If that fails, compare with the server's config.json in Match mods.
Mods only work with the game version they're updated for. After a game update, wait for mods to update.
